difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's proposition at source lines 1323-1326: if M is standard then the map g of the preceeding proposition is the only isomorphism from the standard model to M. The 19-line proof (1328-1346) takes an arbitrary isomorphism h and shows g equals h by induction on n: the base case compares g(0) and h(0) through the interpretation of the constant, and the step computes both sides of a seven-term chain of identities g(n+1) = the value of the numeral n+1 = the successor of the value of the numeral n = the successor of g(n) = the successor of h(n) = h(successor of n) = h(n+1), using the induction hypothesis and the homomorphism property of h (1335-1345). The statement records neither the induction nor the chain, and the map g is defined in the preceeding proposition, which is retained as context.
